# Branch selector: master

To point this chat at a different branch at the user's request, call the branch_select tool - never a checkout of the primary tree. Branch `master` is this chat's inherited pin (the workspace's branch at creation - no explicit pick yet; a UI pick or a branch_select call makes it explicit). It is checked out in the primary tree, so this chat runs in its own per-chat worktree at `.scratch/<CHAT_ID>`, detached at `master`'s tip. The primary tree is the human's — never check it out or move it, and never move `master` from under it. When your task writes to the tree, work in a scratch worktree at this chat's deterministic path, based on the current commit:

`git worktree add .scratch/<CHAT_ID>/run -b run/manifest-<CHAT_ID>`

The harness keeps `.scratch/` git-invisible via the repo's `.git/info/exclude` (#321), so the namespace never shows as untracked noise. Commit there; the run branch carries the work. When the user chooses to land into `master` (ADR-0014 safe-sync SOP, the target is checked out in the primary tree):
1. Only if `git -C <primary worktree> status --porcelain` is EMPTY: `git update-ref refs/heads/master <run tip>` (`git branch -f` REFUSES a checked-out branch - never use it here; plain merges are impossible without checkout), then `git -C <primary> reset --hard master` so the human's tree follows the ref. Any non-empty status: do not move the ref - leave landing to the human and report.
2. If `master` diverged from the run branch, land via plumbing merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree <run base> <run branch>`  - on conflict, do not fake it: report and offer to rebase the run branch onto `master`; on success commit the returned tree with `git commit-tree` (merge commits by agents are allowed per ADR-0014) and move the ref to that commit before the clean-primary checks.
3. Then remove the run worktree (`git worktree remove .scratch/<CHAT_ID>/run && git branch -d run/manifest-<CHAT_ID>`).
A terminal `git switch` on the primary tree changes nothing about this chat's aim - the stored pin, not live HEAD, drives it. New branches derive from this chat's selected branch, never from the primary HEAD. The run branch stays LOCAL: never `git push` it and never open a PR from it - work reaches origin only inside a landed branch, which the human pushes. If a run worktree already exists at that path, it is residue from an earlier run: when it is clean and fully merged into the target, it is landed-and-forgotten — remove it and proceed; when it is dirty or has unmerged commits, leave it untouched, say so, and use `.scratch/<CHAT_ID>/run-2` for this run instead. Typed "land it" or "scrap it" remain the manual fallback for surfaced residue — it is never silently deleted, and never silently blocks a chat. The harness retires a landed-clean chat worktree at run end (#329); if you still see one standing, surface it rather than removing it.

# Scheduled agent: sandbox-only policy

This is an unattended scheduled run with no user to approve anything: read-only tools (search, status checks, observation) still work, but every tool that writes or executes — file edits, bash/powershell, and the sandbox VM tools that install or change anything — comes back as "skipped: approval required". Do not attempt them or retry after a skip. Work read-only: gather information, check status, and report findings, keeping anything disruptive as a recommendation for the user to run themselves.
